lesson.subtitle: Lesson 10 -- That Number Is Wrong
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fábia | Lesson 10 -- That Number Is Wrong

listenings.text: David, thank you for your email about the warehouse line. Before I say anything about the figure, could you confirm which file you have? The one from the fourteenth, or the one from the seventeenth? Good. Two things, then. You are right: the description on that line was not clear, and I will change it. But the amount is correct. The four thousand is a warehouse invoice. It arrived after your export. We will reconcile both files today.

Team, this is David. I have just spoken to our accountants about the warehouse line. She said the four thousand was an invoice. She said it arrived after our export. She asked which file we were looking at. I told her we had the one from the fourteenth. She said they would reconcile both files today. So nobody writes to them until tomorrow.

paras: Fabia, thanks for the report, which we have now been through with the finance team. Most of it lines up with what we have here. There is one item I would like to understand better before we sign it off.

On the warehouse line, your figure and ours differ by roughly four thousand. I am not saying your number is wrong. I am saying the two files do not agree, and I cannot approve a figure I cannot explain to my own board.

Two requests, then. Could you resend the breakdown for that line, and could you tell me where the four thousand comes from? If it is an invoice we have not seen, that would explain it, and I would rather know that today than argue about it next quarter.
One smaller point while I have you. The description on that line reads as if it covers the whole quarter, and I do not think it does. That is what sent us looking in the first place.
reading.source: Client email written for this lesson.

An explanation he can take to his own board, today rather than next quarter.
For the whole report to be reissued with the finance team's numbers.

matching.title: Match the word to its meaning
defs: when two numbers that should match do not
to make two sets of numbers agree, line by line
a formal question about one specific item
to accept the other side is right on one point
to check one source against another
to report a figure as bigger than it really is

items.situation: "Your warehouse figure is wrong." Report it. One sentence.
tips: He said the warehouse figure was wrong.

items.situation: "Can you resend the breakdown?" Report it. One sentence.
tips: He asked whether we could resend the breakdown.

items.situation: "Where does the four thousand come from?" Report it. One sentence.
tips: He wanted to know where the four thousand came from.

items.situation: "We will not approve the report this week." Report it. One sentence.
tips: They said they would not approve the report that week.

items.situation: "We have already checked it against our invoices." Report it. One sentence.
tips: He said they had already checked it against their invoices.

items.situation: Now tell the team what you conceded. One sentence.
tips: I conceded the description, but I stood by the amount.
